narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Reads the lines that introduce each speech.

job.name: Job
job.note: The afflicted just man of Hus, defending his innocence before his friends and God.

2.t: Whose helper art thou? is it of him that is weak? and dost thou hold up the arm of him that has no strength?

3.t: To whom hast thou given counsel? perhaps to him that hath no wisdom, and thou hast shewn thy very great prudence.

4.t: Whom hast thou desired to teach? was it not him that made life?

5.t: Behold the giants groan under the waters, and they that dwell with them.

6.t: Hell is naked before him, and there is no covering for destruction.

7.t: He stretched out the north over the empty space, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.

8.t: He bindeth up the waters in his clouds, so that they break not out and fall down together.

9.t: He withholdeth the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud over it.

10.t: He hath set bounds about the waters, till light and darkness come to an end.

11.t: The pillars of heaven tremble, and dread at his beck.

12.t: By his power the seas are suddenly gathered together, and his wisdom has struck the proud one.

13.t: His spirit hath adorned the heavens, and his obstetric hand brought forth the winding serpent.

14.t: Lo, these things are said in part of his ways: and seeing we have heard scarce a little drop of his word, who shall be able to behold the thunder of his greatness?
